title: Patch: the dungeon fight lists its live modifiers in full, as every other table's rail does
thread: **Issue #3912 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #3912: Patch: the dungeon fight lists its live modifiers in full, as every other table's rail does Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. ## What it actually means Some cards put a lasting effect on a player, such as “Extra turns owed: 1”, “Your next refresh gives 0 mana” or a delayed effect counting down. Every other table has a small chip in its side rail that opens the full list of these effects: online matches, practice, daily games, co-op, watching, replays and the tutorial. On a phone the chip is the only way to read them, because the badges beside the hero are cut short and a touch screen never shows their hover text. A dungeon fight has no such chip. Once this is built, it shows the same chip and list. ## Why - `apps/web/src/game/ModifierList.tsx` (R169) shows every live modifier, in full, one tap from the table's controls. Its header explains why: on a phone the badges are shortened, and their full text is a `title`, which a touch screen never shows. - It sits in the rail of `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, `routes/practice.tsx:1124`, `daily/DailyBoard.tsx:222`, `duos/DuosBoard.tsx`, `together/WatchRoute.tsx`, `replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx` and `tutorial/TutorialHud.tsx`. The daily board's comment reads: every live modifier in full, one tap away, as every other table's rail lists them. - `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx:307-315` passes `matchStatus` with the enemy's name, `RunTimer` and `ThinkIndicator` only, and never imports `ModifierList`. - A fight plays catalog cards, and the engine lists their modifiers in `SideView.modifiers` (`crates/engine/src/view_for.rs`, around 1340-1370: extra turns owed, a 0-mana refresh, delayed effects). ## Proposal Add `ModifierList` to FightScreen's `matchStatus` (`view={snapshot.view}`), with the enemy's translated name as its `opponentLabel`, as practice passes “AI”. Then check that the rail still fits beside the artifact trays at the phone breakpoint. ## Where it lands - `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx`, `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx` - The fight's CSS, only if the rail overflows on a phone - SPEC §15 (dungeon runs); R169 ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A FightScreen test: a view with one modifier in `you.modifiers` shows the `modifier-list` chip with `data-count=1`, and tapping it opens `modifier-list-panel` holding that label. - [ ] A modifier on the enemy's side is listed under the enemy's name. - [ ] With no modifier on either side, no chip renders. - [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and the touched test files pass. ## Size and risks Small: a few lines plus two or three tests. The only risk is crowding the fight's rail on a phone, and the chip renders nothing while no modifier is live. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `claude-7` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43666355951)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal A dungeon fight's board rail shows the same live-modifier chip and list as every other table. `FightScreen` renders `ModifierList` in its `matchStatus`, with the enemy's translated name as `opponentLabel`. The chip appears only while a modifier is live on either side. The rail must still fit on a phone. Requirements, from the issue's acceptance criteria: - A `you.modifiers` entry shows the `modifier-list` chip with `data-count=1`, and tapping it opens `modifier-list-panel` holding the label. - An enemy-side modifier is listed under the enemy's name. - No modifier on either side means no chip. - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and the touched test files pass. The spec does not say a fight lists modifiers, so this takes a ruling (CLAUDE.md rule 3). It is **R3912000**, following the precedent of R3855000, which did the same for the daily board. ## Files to touch | File | Change | |---|---| | `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx` | change: import `ModifierList`. Make `matchStatus` a fragment: the chip first, then the existing `dungeon-fight__status` span. Update the header comment. | | `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx` | change: `snapshotFor` and `fightHost` take an optional modifiers argument. Add `describe("R3912000 …")` with 4 tests. | | `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/fight.css` | change: one comment (line 115) only, to say the chip sits in the rail. No rule changes. | | `spec/rulings/R3912000.md` | new: the ruling note. | | `spec/pending/3912.md` | new: the §11 paragraph. The `spec/pending/` directory is absent now, so writing the file creates it. | | `spec/15-dungeon-run.md` | change: one sentence in §15.6, in the paragraph beginning "The game seed is the run's seed". | | `apps/web/README.md` | change: one clause in the paragraph at line 1021 that lists where the chip shows. | Do not touch these: - Anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` or `.claude/`. - `crates/**`, including the engine. - `apps/web/src/game/ModifierList.tsx`, `modifierList.css` and `board.css`. - `spec/11-rulings.md` and `spec/INDEX.md`. Never run `cargo jackioh spec index`; a daily job does it. - `e2e/`. - Any catalog or patch fragment. This is not a card change, so none is needed. Governing: SPEC §15.6, §10.8, R169 (modifiers travel in the view on both seats), R2706000 (a fight is a practice game), R3855000 (precedent), CLAUDE.md rules 3 and 7. ## Steps 1. **`apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx`, import.** - Add `import { ModifierList } from "../../game/ModifierList.tsx";` directly after the line `import { CatalogContext, lookupFromDefs } from "../../game/catalog.ts";`. 2. **Same file, `matchStatus` prop (currently lines 307-315).** Replace the prop's value with a fragment. Keep the `…` block exactly as it is, and put `ModifierList` before it: ```tsx matchStatus={ <> {/* R3912000: every live modifier in full, as every other table's rail lists them (R169), the enemy's name over its list. Beside the text, not inside it: the chip is 32px tall and the text wraps, so inside it a phone's one-row control bar would grow a line taller. */} …unchanged… } ``` - `enemy` (`const enemy = t(setup.enemy.name)`, line 248) is already in scope. Do not call `t()` again. - `.practice-table .board-status` (`practice/practice.css:1481`) is already a centered flex row with an 8px gap. It applies because the board wrapper is `practice-board practice-table`. So the chip centers beside the text with no CSS. - The chip goes first so that, on a very narrow screen, `.board-status`'s `overflow: hidden` clips the end of a long enemy name rather than the chip. This is also practice's order (`routes/practice.tsx:1124`). 3. **Same file, header comment (lines 3-6).** - Change "whose name the board's rail shows beside the run's timer (B22, B24)" to "…beside the run's timer and the chip that lists the live modifiers (B22, B24, R3912000)". Keep the line breaks tidy. 4. **`apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/fight.css`, line 115 comment.** - Change `/* The board's rail: the enemy's name, the run's time and "AI is thinking…". */` to `/* The board's rail, a centered row (practice.css): the modifier chip when any is live (R3912000), then the enemy's name, the run's time and "AI is thinking…". */`. - Change no rule. The chip beside the wrapping text keeps the row at one line on a phone, so no CSS is needed. The issue allows a CSS change "only if the rail overflows". 5. **`apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx`, test plumbing.** - Imports: - Add `import type { ModifierView } from "@jackioh/shared";` with the other package imports, below the `@jackioh/run` type import. - Add `import { modifierListTestid } from "../../game/ModifierList.tsx";` next to the `ConfirmConcede` import. - Extend the fixtures import to `import { baseView, emptySide, opponentModifiers, yourModifiers } from "../../test/fixtures.ts";`. - Add a type above `snapshotFor`: `/** The modifiers each side's view lists (R169). */ type SideModifiers = { you?: ModifierView[]; opponent?: ModifierView[] };` - Change the signature to `snapshotFor(result = null, aiToAct = false, modifiers: SideModifiers = {})`. Build the two sides as `emptySide("p1", { modifiers: modifiers.you ?? [] })` and `emptySide("p2", { hand: { count: 4 }, modifiers: modifiers.opponent ?? [] })`. - Add a fifth parameter to `fightHost`: `modifiers: SideModifiers = {}`. Pass `modifiers` as the third argument at all four `snapshotFor(...)` calls inside `host.request`: the default snapshot, the `resume` "started" one, the `start` one and the concede one. Say "(R169)" in the parameter's doc comment. 6. **Same file, new `describe`.** Add it after `describe("B24 the run's timer on screen", …)`. Every title starts with `R3912000` so `cargo jackioh spec check` finds the proof. Use the pattern at `routes/practice.test.tsx:2412` and `daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx:318`. Each test calls `renderFight(fightHost([], false, "failed", 0, {…}), fakeDungeon(vi.fn(() => null)))`, then `await screen.findByTestId(fightTestid.screen)`. ## Tests File: `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx`, `describe("R3912000 a fight's rail lists the live modifiers (R169)", …)`. 1. `it("R3912000 a modifier on your side shows the chip in the rail, and tapping it lists the label under You")` - Modifiers: `{ you: [yourModifiers[0]] }`. `yourModifiers[0]` is a fixture entry; `yourModifiers` has 2 entries. - `chip = screen.getByTestId(modifierListTestid.chip)` has `data-count="1"`. - `chip.closest(".modifier-list")?.parentElement` has class `board-status`. This pins the placement beside the text. - `chip.closest(".dungeon-fight__status")` is `null`. - `queryByTestId(modifierListTestid.panel)` is `null` before the click. - After `fireEvent.click(chip)`, the panel has the text `yourModifiers[0].label`, and its `.modifier-list__who` texts equal `["You"]`. 2. `it("R3912000 a modifier on the enemy's side is listed under the enemy's name")` - Modifiers: `{ opponent: opponentModifiers }`. - Chip `data-count` is `String(opponentModifiers.length)`. Click it. - `panel.querySelector('[data-side="opponent"] .modifier-list__who')` has text `"Cave Troll"`. This equals `screen.getByTestId(fightTestid.enemy).textContent`. - That side element contains `opponentModifiers[0].label`. - `panel.querySelector('[data-side="you"]')` is `null`. 3. `it("R3912000 a modifier on each side is counted together and listed under each name")` - Modifiers: `{ you: yourModifiers, opponent: opponentModifiers }`. - `data-count` is `String(yourModifiers.length + opponentModifiers.length)`. - After the click, the `.modifier-list__who` texts are `["You", "Cave Troll"]`, and every label appears in the panel. 4. `it("R3912000 with no modifier on either side no chip renders")` - Use the default `fightHost()`. - `screen.queryByTestId(modifierListTestid.chip)` is `null`, and so is `screen.queryByTestId(modifierListTestid.panel)`. The existing tests need no change. B24's `timer.closest(".board-status")` still holds. The `closest(".hero-aside")` tests are untouched. Commands, in this order: ``` pnpm --dir apps/web test src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/ModifierList.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/dungeon/fight cargo jackioh spec check ``` - `pnpm … test` runs `build-wasm.sh` first via `pretest`, which is slow once. - If `git rev-parse origin/main` resolves, also run `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`. It should report no card change and no claims. If `origin/main` is missing, skip it and say so in the report. ## Spec and docs (do after the code) 7. **`spec/rulings/R3912000.md`**, new. Front matter: ``` --- id: R3912000 title: "A dungeon fight's board rail lists the live modifiers, as every other table's does (issue #3912, amends R169)" cards: "§10.8, §15.6, R169, R2706000, R3855000, issue #3912" proven_in: - apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx --- ``` Body, in the style of R3855000's: - R169 put each side's modifiers in the view. The chip beside the board's controls lists them in full, because on a phone the badges are cut short and a touch screen never shows a `title`. - A fight is a practice game ([[R2706000]]), but its rail passed `matchStatus` only the enemy's name, the run's timer and the thinking indicator. So no chip appeared there, though a fight plays catalog cards that install modifiers. - The fight's rail now carries the chip while any modifier is live on either side, headed You and the enemy's name, with the chip beside the rail's text. - Presentation only: it reads `SideView.modifiers` of the viewer's own `view`, nothing else and nothing hidden (CLAUDE.md rule 7). - "Hearthstone semantics: the board's information is the same at every table." - Rejected: the chip inside the wrapping text span, whose 32px height would grow a phone's one-row control bar. Also rejected: the heading "Opponent" or "AI" over the enemy's list, since the rail already names the enemy. - Link every ruling and section with `[[R…]]` or `[[§…]]`. Write plain numbers for everything else. 8. **`spec/pending/3912.md`**, new, one paragraph in the shape of `spec/pending/3855.md`: - `**[[R3912000]] A dungeon fight's board rail lists the live modifiers (issue #3912, 2026-11-15)**: amends [[R169]]. …` - Say that a fight's rail carried no chip, that it now carries `ModifierList` under You and the enemy's name, that it is presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7), and what was rejected. End with "It takes R3912000 and edits [[§15.6]]." 9. **`spec/15-dungeon-run.md`**, §15.6. Edit the paragraph that starts "The game seed is the run's seed, row and column." Replace the end of it, `Leaving still asks first ([[R2706000]], [[R2972000]]).`, with `Leaving still asks first ([[R2706000]], [[R2972000]]). The fight's rail lists every live modifier in full, under You and the enemy's name, as every other table's does ([[R3912000]], [[R169]]).` 10. **`apps/web/README.md`**, line 1021 paragraph. - Replace `Practice and the lessons show the same chip in their HUD, under You and AI, the Duos board shows it` with `Practice and the lessons show the same chip in their HUD, under You and AI, a dungeon fight's rail shows it under You and the enemy's name (R3912000), the Duos board shows it`. ## Done when - [ ] `FightScreen` renders the chip while any modifier is live, with `data-count` giving the total across both sides. - [ ] Tapping the chip opens `modifier-list-panel` with the label under You and, for the enemy's, under the enemy's name. - [ ] No chip renders with no modifier on either side. - [ ] All four R3912000 tests and the existing FightScreen tests pass, and `ModifierList.test.tsx` still passes. - [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint on `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight` are clean. - [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` is clean. - [ ] The ruling note, the pending paragraph, the §15.6 sentence and the README clause are in. - [ ] No `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, lint disable or `@ts-*` comment was added. - [ ] The final report names the commands actually run and their results. It also says plainly that the phone layout was reasoned from the stylesheets, unless it was looked at in a browser. The harness then runs its own checks: `cargo fmt --check`, catalog, patches, clippy, the workspace tests and the changed web tests. Nothing in this change touches Rust, the catalog or `wire/`, so those should pass untouched. ## Risks - **Phone rail fit.** The chip is `min-height: 32px`. Inside the wrapping `.dungeon-fight__status` span it would likely wrap to its own line, and the one-row control bar (`board.css:3497`, `nowrap`) would grow about 14px. The card-height budget there assumes a 44px row. The chip is therefore a sibling beside the span, vertically centered by `.practice-table .board-status`, and test 1 pins that placement. In the worst case, a long boss name on a ~390px screen has its end clipped by `.board-status { overflow: hidden }`. The chip stays visible because it is first. - **Optional visual check.** The `ui-walkthrough` skill could look at a fight at 390×844. Booting a dungeon run in a browser is costly, so skip it unless it is cheap. The issue's acceptance criteria are the tests and typecheck. - **The list is clipped.** It is not. The panel is portaled to `document.body` and fixed, so `.board-status`'s `overflow: hidden` does not clip it. This is the same as at every other table. - **Hidden information.** `snapshot.view` is the viewer's own `PlayerView`, so nothing new crosses the boundary (rule 7). The enemy's modifiers are already public in the view (R169). - **Duplicate test ids.** `Board.tsx:802` renders `matchStatus` once, so there is one chip. `ModifierList` is not rendered anywhere else on the fight screen. - **`spec check` failures.** The test titles must contain the literal `R3912000`. The note's `proven_in` file must exist. Every `[[…]]` link must resolve. The `cards:` entries (`§10.8`, `§15.6`, `R169`, `R2706000`, `R3855000`) all exist. A comment citing `R3912000` in `FightScreen.tsx` is valid only once the note exists, so do the spec steps in the same change. ## Open questions None. The one judgment call is making the ruling note and spec edit part of this change. The issue lists "SPEC §15; R169" under "Where it lands", and R3855000 set the precedent. The builder should record that choice, and the rejected alternative of citing R169 only with no new note, in its report. --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-11-15T02:06:31Z: approve ````
